the design and development of systems which can assist decision makers to identify the key factors which may lead to a particular event (such as a terrorist attack) occurring.
the design and implementation of a new generation of systems for scenario modelling and analysis, which can be used for detecting and preventing serious crime (e. g. terrorism) in a timely manner.
the development of a methodology for the generation and analysis of scenarios for the detection and prevention of crime.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that fuzzy set theory, rough set theory, and their integration can be used for the development of a number of intelligent decision support systems for the prevention of serious crime, including terrorism.

we have developed a novel and effective methodology to support the generation of scenarios from a given set of intelligence data and the subsequent assessment of these scenarios in terms of their plausibility and potential impact.
we have demonstrated that the use of fuzzy set and rough set theories can be used to generate a number of scenarios which can explain the given intelligence data.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of fuzzy sets and rough sets can provide a powerful and flexible tool for modelling and analysing complex data and for generating plausible scenarios which can help to identify and prevent serious crimes.
the integration of fuzzy sets and rough sets provides an effective framework for modelling and analysis of intelligence data.
the integration of fuzzy and rough set theory can lead to more effective and efficient scenario modelling and analysis, and hence more effective and efficient decision support systems.
